# signal-summarizer

A Signal bot that catches you up on a chat. Ask it in the conversation:

```
!summarize          # the last 24 hours
!summarize 90m      # the last 90 minutes
!summarize 7d       # the last 7 days
!summarize 50       # the last 50 messages
!help
```

It replies in the same chat with a plain-text summary: what was discussed,
what was decided, who owes what, and what is still open.

**Summaries are generated by a local model by default** — Ollama or any
OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, llamafile) — so message
text never leaves the machine the bot runs on. The Claude API is available as
an opt-in backend when you want a stronger model and accept sending
transcripts off the box.

It works in group chats and in direct messages, keeps its own history in a
local SQLite file, and can also post a scheduled digest from cron.

## How it fits together

```
Signal ──► signal-cli daemon ──JSON-RPC──► signal-summarizer ──► SQLite
                    ▲                             │
                    │                             ▼
                    │                    Ollama / llama.cpp on localhost
                    └──────── summary ────────────┘        (or the Claude API)
```

`signal-cli` owns the Signal protocol, registration, and encryption. This bot
talks to its JSON-RPC socket: it records incoming messages and, when someone
runs a command, sends the recent transcript to the model and posts the reply.

**It can only summarize messages it saw while running.** Signal has no
server-side history to backfill from.

## Setup

### 1. Install and link signal-cli

Install [signal-cli](https://github.com/AsamK/signal-cli) (`brew install
signal-cli`, or the release tarball on Linux), then either link the bot to an
existing Signal account as a second device:

```bash
signal-cli link -n "summarizer-bot"   # prints a tsdevice:/ URI — turn it into a
                                      # QR code and scan it from Signal ▸ Linked devices
```

…or register a separate number for the bot:

```bash
signal-cli -a +15551234567 register       # add --voice if SMS does not arrive
signal-cli -a +15551234567 verify 123456
```

A linked device sees the chats of the account it is linked to, which is
usually what you want for summarizing your own group chats.

### 2. Start the daemon

```bash
signal-cli -a +15551234567 daemon --tcp 127.0.0.1:7583
```

A UNIX socket works too (`--socket /run/signal-cli.sock`); point
`SIGNAL_RPC_ADDRESS` at `unix:///run/signal-cli.sock`. Keep the socket bound
to localhost — anyone who can reach it can send messages as your account.

### 3. Set up the local model

With [Ollama](https://ollama.com) (the default backend):

```bash
ollama serve &                 # usually already running as a service
ollama pull llama3.2:3b        # ~2 GB; see the table below for other sizes
```

Or with llama.cpp's `llama-server`, LM Studio, vLLM, or anything else that
speaks the OpenAI chat API:

```bash
llama-server -m qwen2.5-7b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf -c 16384 --port 8080
export SUMMARIZER_BACKEND=openai        # endpoint defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
export EDGE_CONTEXT_TOKENS=16384        # match the -c you started the server with
```

### 4. Install the bot

```bash
cd signal-summarizer
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

The edge backends use only the standard library. `anthropic` is installed as a
dependency but is imported only if you select the Claude backend.

### 5. Configure and check

```bash
export SIGNAL_ACCOUNT=+15551234567
export SIGNAL_RPC_ADDRESS=tcp://127.0.0.1:7583
export SUMMARIZER_DB=~/.local/share/signal-summarizer.db
export EDGE_MODEL=llama3.2:3b

signal-summarizer check
```

`check` confirms the model server is reachable, that the model is installed,
and how long a round trip takes:

```
backend:   ollama llama3.2:3b at http://127.0.0.1:11434
transcript budget: 23688 characters per model call
status:    ollama reachable at http://127.0.0.1:11434, model llama3.2:3b installed
test call: ok in 0.6s - the summarizer is ready
Message text stays on this machine with this backend.
```

### 6. Run

```bash
signal-summarizer run          # or: python -m signal_summarizer run
```

Send `!help` in any chat the account is in to confirm it is alive.

## Choosing a local model

Summarizing is an easy task for a small model as long as the conversation fits
in its context window. Rough guidance:

| RAM / VRAM | Model | `EDGE_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4–8 GB | `llama3.2:3b`, `gemma3:4b`, `qwen3:4b` | 8192 | Fine for a day of a normal group chat |
| 8–16 GB | `qwen2.5:7b`, `mistral:7b`, `gemma3:12b` | 16384 | Noticeably better at attributing who said what |
| 16 GB+ | `qwen2.5:14b`, `gemma3:27b`, `llama3.3:70b` | 32768+ | Closest to hosted-model quality |

Two things matter more than raw parameter count:

- **Context window.** `EDGE_CONTEXT_TOKENS` must match what the server is
  actually serving. Ollama defaults to a small context regardless of what the
  model supports, so the bot sends `num_ctx` explicitly — but the value it
  sends is this setting, and setting it higher than the model can handle makes
  the runtime truncate the transcript silently.
- **Instruction following.** Prefer instruct/chat-tuned builds. Reasoning
  models (`qwen3`, `deepseek-r1`) work too; their `<think>` blocks are stripped
  before the summary is posted, but they spend tokens and time thinking, so
  raise `EDGE_OUTPUT_TOKENS` and `EDGE_TIMEOUT` if you use one.

### Long windows on a small context

When a requested window does not fit in one model call, the bot splits the
transcript into consecutive chunks, summarizes each, then combines those
partial summaries into one (repeating that fold if there are many). So
`!summarize 7d` works on a 3B model — it just makes several calls instead of
one. Watch for `summarizing in N chunks` in the logs; if N is regularly large,
a bigger context window is the fix.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SIGNAL_ACCOUNT` | *(required)* | The number signal-cli is registered or linked to |
| `SIGNAL_RPC_ADDRESS` | `tcp://127.0.0.1:7583` | `tcp://host:port` or `unix:///path/to.sock` |
| `SUMMARIZER_DB` | `signal-summarizer.db` | SQLite file for message history |
| `SUMMARIZER_BACKEND` | `ollama` | `ollama`, `openai` (llama.cpp/LM Studio/vLLM), or `claude` |
| `SUMMARIZER_PREFIX` | `!` | Command prefix |
| `SUMMARIZER_WINDOW_HOURS` | `24` | Default window for a bare `!summarize` |
| `SUMMARIZER_MAX_MESSAGES` | `400` | Cap on messages fed to one summary |
| `SUMMARIZER_MAX_CHARS` | *(derived)* | Transcript characters per model call; defaults to a value derived from the context window |
| `SUMMARIZER_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | History older than this is deleted |
| `SUMMARIZER_ALLOWED_CHATS` | *(all)* | Comma-separated chat ids to restrict the bot to |

Edge backends (`ollama`, `openai`):

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EDGE_ENDPOINT` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (ollama), `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (openai) | Model server base URL; `OLLAMA_HOST` is honoured too |
| `EDGE_MODEL` | `llama3.2:3b` | Model name as the server knows it |
| `EDGE_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | `8192` | Context window to request; drives the transcript budget |
| `EDGE_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `1024` | Cap on summary length |
| `EDGE_TEMPERATURE` | `0.2` | Low keeps summaries factual |
| `EDGE_TIMEOUT` | `300` | Seconds to wait for one generation |
| `EDGE_API_KEY` | *(none)* | Bearer token, if your server requires one |

Claude backend (`SUMMARIZER_BACKEND=claude`):

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | *(from SDK auth)* | API key, if you are not using an `ant auth login` profile |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `claude-opus-5` | Model id |
| `ANTHROPIC_EFFORT` | `medium` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max` |
| `ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS` | `4000` | Output cap for a summary |
| `ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS` | `1` | Server-side refusal fallbacks; `0` disables |

Chat ids look like `group:<base64 group id>` or `dm:+15551234567`. Run
`signal-summarizer chats` to list the ones it has seen.

## Scheduled digests

`digest` summarizes one chat and prints it; `--send` posts it back to the chat.
For a 08:00 weekday digest:

```cron
0 8 * * 1-5 cd /opt/signal-summarizer && .venv/bin/signal-summarizer digest \
    --chat 'group:Zm9vYmFy' --hours 24 --send >> /var/log/signal-digest.log 2>&1
```

The cron job needs the same environment variables as `run` and can share the
same database file while the bot is running.

## Running as a service

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/signal-summarizer.service
[Unit]
Description=Signal chat summarizer
After=network-online.target signal-cli.service ollama.service
Requires=signal-cli.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=signal
WorkingDirectory=/opt/signal-summarizer
EnvironmentFile=/etc/signal-summarizer.env
ExecStart=/opt/signal-summarizer/.venv/bin/signal-summarizer run
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

## Notes on behavior

- **Privacy.** With an edge backend, transcripts go only to the model server at
  `EDGE_ENDPOINT` — keep that on localhost and nothing leaves the machine.
  Either way, message bodies are stored in plaintext in the SQLite file: keep it
  on an encrypted disk with restrictive permissions, set
  `SUMMARIZER_RETENTION_DAYS` to the shortest window you can live with, and tell
  the group the bot is there. With `SUMMARIZER_BACKEND=claude`, the transcript
  for the requested window is sent to the Anthropic API on every summary.
- **Scope.** `SUMMARIZER_ALLOWED_CHATS` restricts both recording and commands
  to specific chats. Anyone in an allowed chat can run `!summarize` for that
  chat only.
- **Failures.** If the model server is down or slow, the bot says so in the chat
  and puts the endpoint and error in its logs rather than in the group.
- **Refusals** (Claude backend). Claude Opus 5's safety classifiers can decline
  a request. The bot enables server-side fallbacks (`fallbacks: "default"`), so
  a declined request is retried on Anthropic's recommended fallback model; if
  that also declines, the bot says so in the chat. `ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS=0`
  turns it off.
- **Reconnects.** If signal-cli restarts, the bot reconnects with exponential
  backoff (up to 60s) and keeps its history.

## Development

```bash
python -m pytest
```

The tests cover envelope parsing, the message store, command handling, the
JSON-RPC client (against a stub daemon on a real socket), both edge backends
(against a stub HTTP model server), chunked map-reduce summarization, the CLI,
and an end-to-end pass from Signal socket to local model and back. No network
access, API key, or local model is required to run them.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `signal_summarizer/signal_client.py` | JSON-RPC client for the signal-cli daemon |
| `signal_summarizer/envelope.py` | signal-cli envelopes → flat message records |
| `signal_summarizer/store.py` | SQLite history |
| `signal_summarizer/summarizer.py` | Prompts, chunking, and combining partial summaries |
| `signal_summarizer/backends/edge.py` | Ollama and OpenAI-compatible local models |
| `signal_summarizer/backends/claude.py` | Anthropic Messages API |
| `signal_summarizer/bot.py` | Commands, replies, and the listen loop |
| `signal_summarizer/cli.py` | `run`, `check`, `chats`, `digest` |
